title: Cross-SDK credential conduit and pullstream ergonomics alignment (py/ts/go) + version bumps
author: Evan Chen
release_notes: Aligned credential lifecycle and streaming ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Introduced credential conduit abstraction, pauseable pullstream helpers, documented backoff defaults; bumped SDK versions (py:1.12.0, ts:2.7.0, go:1.9.0).
description: Context and motivation: Customers reported subtle mismatches between SDKs when recovering long-lived streaming sessions after auth refreshes and when applying retry windows. That caused duplicated reconnect logic in application code and intermittent token-exchange races during prefilling/heartbeat flows. This PR implements a lightweight cross-SDK credential conduit and a small set of ergonomic pullstream helpers to make authentication transitions (rotate, prefetch, drain) observable and consistent between Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Summary of work: - Introduced a credential_conduit / CredentialConduit abstraction (language idiomatic wrappers) that centralizes token lookup, priming, and optional lease semantics. - Added PauseablePullstream / PauseableAsyncIterator / PullStream.Pause helpers so consumers can checkpoint/prime/cooldown without ad-hoc buffering. - Standardized retry profile defaults used by streaming reconnects (latency-aware backoff with small hedging window). - Harmonized telemetry labels emitted from auth/stream transitions so backend traces can aggregate cross-language. - Minor public surface tweaks for ergonomics: clearer javadocs/docstrings on session pinning, added transient_error sentinel for typed errors. - Version bumps: python-sdk -> 1.12.0, typescript-sdk -> 2.7.0, go-sdk -> 1.9.0. Compatibility notes: This change is additive. Existing auth flows continue to work. Consumers who used internal/undocumented token hooks should migrate to the conduit API for improved correctness; migration notes included in CHANGELOGs. Test plan and verification: Unit tests added for credential conduit priming and pause/resume semantics in all three SDKs. Integration tests exercised streaming reconnects against the local mock server with token rotation scenarios. We also ran a limited canary of the TS SDK in staging (5% traffic) for 48 hours and observed zero increase in reconnects; latency tail improved slightly for long-duration sessions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-9123) - [x] unit tests for py/ts/go - [x] integration tests with mock server - [x] docs/CHANGELOG updates - [x] release notes drafted - [x] package publish scripts validated Rollout: Merged to main. SDK packages will be published as part of the coordinated release job: py v1.12.0, ts v2.7.0, go v1.9.0. Followups: - expose an opt-in telemetry flag to increase conduit diagnostics (ENG-9270) - document patterns for graceful session handoff in Redwood Console examples.
